charts.census_oldest: Oldest open work has been sitting in its stage for up to {age} (p90).

settings.title: Settings
settings.board_hint: Where this project's tasks start when the API or an agent creates them without naming a board. A task created from the board starts on the board that is open.
settings.description_hint: the agent reads this at init
settings.description_placeholder: Public website (Next.js). Marketing copy, landing pages, A/B tests.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.note: Removes the local clone and all worktrees. Tasks linked to it lose their project.
danger.confirm_message: Removes the local clone and all worktrees. Tasks linked to it will lose their project.

github.title: GitHub access
github.credential_hint: one of the workspace's, stored on the credentials page
github.linked_html: Linked to GitHub App installation {installation} — tokens minted on demand.
github.app_decides: The App installation above is what clones and pushes.
github.app_outranks: The App installation above is what clones and pushes. Unlink it to use a credential instead.
github.uses_credential: Clones, pushes and pull requests use this credential.
github.no_credential: No credential yet — the repo has to be public to clone.
github.no_credentials: No GitHub credentials in this workspace yet. Add one on the credentials page.
github.unlink_message: The project falls back to its stored credential, or to public access. The App stays installed on GitHub.
github.link_hint: Link this project to the App. Thulu checks that the installation reaches the repository.

environments.title: Environments
environments.intro: Where this repo actually runs. Naming the deployments is what lets an agent ask about {em} error rate instead of the project's in the abstract — and keeps a dev blip from reading like an incident. Cloud credentials are stored encrypted and resolved server-side; agents never see them.
environments.empty: No environments yet. Add one to describe where this repo runs.
environments.approve_message: They start feeding the panel on the next collection pass, and any mapping they replace is retired. Reversible.
environments.metric_approved: Metric approved — it can be charted now
environments.metric_delete_message: Its stored points go too. If the app keeps sending it, it comes back as waiting.
environments.collected_nothing: Collected — nothing to record (no traffic in the window)
environments.saved_without_credential: Environment saved, but the credential was not attached: {error}
environments.delete_message_with_credential: Its stored cloud credential is deleted too. Its Evidence runs and videos stay, under Other sites. This cannot be undone.
environments.delete_message: Its Evidence runs and videos stay, under Other sites. This cannot be undone.

env_form.system_hint: same value across repos of one deployment
env_form.provider_hint: Only AWS and Google Cloud are read today. The other two can be recorded, but no metrics will be collected for them.
env_form.account_hint: AWS account id or GCP project id
env_form.selectors_hint: one key=value per line, narrows resources
env_form.cred_resolves: Cloud tools resolve this key when an agent names this environment.
env_form.cred_none_for_provider: No credential for this provider yet — pick “New credential…” to add one.
env_form.cred_name_or_none: Name the credential, or pick “— none —”
env_form.display_name_hint: shown in Evidence instead of the name
env_form.production_hint: Stricter thresholds; a regression here is an incident

credentials.title: Cloud credential
credentials.intro: Pick a credential from the workspace. Environments do not store keys — they point at one, so the same key can serve several environments and is validated, monitored and revoked in a single place. Manage the keys themselves on the {link} page.
credentials.validated_hint: Validated against the provider before it is stored, and granted to this environment on save.
credentials.none_in_workspace: No credentials in this workspace yet — pick “New credential…” to add one.
credentials.none_for_provider: No {provider} credential exists yet — pick “New credential…” to add one.
credentials.resolves: Agents working on this project resolve {credential} for {environment}.
credentials.nothing_granted: Nothing is granted yet, so cloud tools have no credential for {environment}.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.intro: Point an OpenTelemetry SDK or collector here and this environment's tiles fill in from the application itself — per-request latency and errors that no cloud API can see. The token is write-only: it can send telemetry and nothing else.
telemetry.copy_now: Copy this now — it is not shown again.
telemetry.name_required: Give the token a name: it is how you tell collectors apart below.
telemetry.address_fallback: Settings has no Telemetry address, so this uses this browser's ({origin}). If the app runs somewhere that cannot reach it, an operator sets the address in Settings › API.
telemetry.sources_hint: Every address that has presented a token, accepted or refused. A refusal is almost always an allowlist that no longer matches — a NAT gateway changing address is the usual cause, and the only symptom otherwise is tiles that quietly stop filling in.
telemetry.cidr_help: Leave it empty to accept from anywhere: the default, and the right choice for autoscaled infrastructure where the outbound address is not fixed.
telemetry.revoke_message: Anything still using it stops reporting immediately, and it cannot be un-revoked.

dashboards.title: Dashboard
dashboards.publish_message: It becomes the environment's live dashboard and any active version with the same name is archived. Reversible.
dashboards.discard_message: The panels go; the metrics and their history stay.
dashboards.delete_message: The dashboard stops showing for everyone. The metrics and their history stay.

stage_files.panel_note: One prompt and one pre-launch hook per stage. The agent gets them when it starts on this project, next to the init script.
stage_files.title: Stage files
stage_files.discard_message: You have unsaved edits in this file.
stage_files.prune_message: Removes {files} from this project's stage files folder. This cannot be undone.
stage_files.edits_lost: Edits to this file will be lost.
stage_files.delete_message: This removes the file from the project.

init_script.title: Init script
init_script.intro: The script that brings this project up inside a task's sandbox. Agents run it with init_run instead of installing and guessing, and when it breaks on an incompatibility they fix it here as a new revision. Every save, yours or an agent's, stays in the history.

code.title: Code
code.intro: This project's code lives in Thulu. Download a branch (a task's shows under its title once the task was merged or published), or upload a new version of the folder as a commit on the default branch.
code.drop_title: Drop the project folder or a .zip here
code.replace_note: The upload replaces what's on {branch}: files missing from the folder are deleted in that commit. Earlier commits stay in the history. A folder from a .zip downloaded here knows its commit: if {branch} moved since, Thulu asks before overwriting.
code.history_ignored: The folder's .git is ignored: the project keeps its own history.
code.uploaded_merged: New commit {version} with the folder, integrated into {branch} by merge {commit}.
code.unchanged: Nothing changed on {branch}: the folder matches the last commit.

moved.explain: Your folder came from an earlier commit. Merge brings what landed on {branch} since and puts your changes on top; replace makes {branch} exactly your folder, undoing those commits.
moved.conflict_explain: Those files changed both in your folder and on the branch. Download the branch again, bring your changes into it and upload that, or replace the branch with your folder.

clone.cloning: The repository is cloning. Tasks can use the project once it is ready; this page updates on its own.
clone.failed: The repository could not be cloned: {reason}. Delete the project and create it again once the cause is fixed.
